pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: The experimental `unstable_Activity` API now has its own React element symbol and reconciler work tag instead of being an alias for Offscreen. Client reconciliation represents Activity as a distinct outer fiber backed by an Offscreen child, server rendering sends it through the existing Offscreen renderer, and DevTools/component naming now exposes it as `Activity`.

behavior_changes.description: Consumers of `unstable_Activity` now receive the dedicated `react.activity` element type rather than the Offscreen type. The new type is accepted as a valid React element type, so Activity has a distinct observable identity while remaining renderable.
evidence: ReactSymbols assigns Activity its own globally registered symbol.
Element-type validation explicitly accepts the Activity symbol.

behavior_changes.description: On the client, an Activity element is represented by a dedicated Activity fiber whose `mode`, children, and ref are forwarded to an Offscreen child. Updates continue through that child rather than treating Activity itself as an Offscreen fiber.
evidence: The element-type switch creates an Activity fiber for REACT_ACTIVITY_TYPE.
Activity reconciliation constructs Offscreen props from Activity mode and children.
The Activity fiber has a distinct numeric work tag.

behavior_changes.description: Server rendering recognizes the new Activity type and renders it through the same Offscreen path used for Offscreen elements.
evidence: The server element dispatch groups REACT_ACTIVITY_TYPE with REACT_OFFSCREEN_TYPE and invokes renderOffscreen.

behavior_changes.description: Developer tooling and component-stack naming can now identify the dedicated fiber as `Activity`, and DevTools treats that fiber as a non-user-code wrapper when deciding whether it should be inspected as an element.
evidence: Both reconciler naming and DevTools display naming return Activity for the new work tag.
DevTools includes Activity among wrapper/host-like tags in its element filtering logic.

local_risks.description: The experimental export now has a different symbol identity from Offscreen. Consumers that persisted, compared, switched on, or manually constructed the previous Offscreen-backed Activity type may no longer recognize it, even though rendering support for the new symbol has been added.

The numeric work-tag assignment is duplicated across the reconciler and DevTools' version-specific mapping. Those values and the version threshold must remain synchronized or DevTools can classify or filter fibers incorrectly for affected renderer versions.

Client reconciliation introduces an extra Activity wrapper around an Offscreen child, while server rendering directly reuses the Offscreen rendering path. Hydration and tree-identity assumptions should be checked where code depends on wrapper structure, refs, or component-stack ownership.
